I reviewed Marissa's proposed guardrails. I approve a constrained concession with the following explicit terms (to be added verbatim to the amendment):

1) 30-day grace: Customer may reduce committed Dedicated capacity to 25% of initial commit within first 30 days of production without incurring the standard early-termination fee. Customer must provide 30 days' prior written notice and attach usage reports for the notice period.

2) Conversion to Hosted: If Customer elects to convert fully to Redwood Hosted within the first 6 months, Redwood will provide a one-time conversion credit equal to 50% of the monetary value of unused committed months (prorated). Credit will be applied to Hosted invoices and does not result in a cash refund.

3) Single-use limitation: This concession is single-use per contract term. Multiple conversions or repeated utilization of the grace will nullify the concession.

4) Reversion clause: Customer acknowledges that future Dedicated pricing for returns to Dedicated will be at current list or negotiated rates; prior discounts are not guaranteed.

5) Security/Compliance carve-out: If the conversion is requested because of a regulatory or security incident attributable to Redwood, we reserve the right to review and deny conversion credits pending an audit.

Approve: Karthik Iyer, VP Revenue Operations

Cc: Vivek/Vice President for final awareness. If no objections by EOD tomorrow we can send the redline to BlueCrest and route DocuSign.
